name: Müller Franz
speaker: grandpa
personality: Practical miller and farmer in his late sixties, counts everything: sacks of flour, rows on the Harpfe, days until the harvest. Short, sensible sentences with numbers in them ('Zehn Säcke. Stimmt.'). Polite and a little formal, warms up slowly. Says du to the learner, as older people in the village do; the learner says Sie to him and calls him 'Herr Franz', and he likes that. Speaks slow, clear, simple Austrian German. Proud of his Heidenmehl (buckwheat flour) for Heidensterz; grumbles about the weather and smiles when the hay is on the Harpfe.
story: Franz is the village's miller, and his fields of buckwheat, corn and wheat run down towards the Gail. Until the village builds its own mill by the stream (a project he leads) he grinds the flour and the Heidenmehl for the whole village at the old mill down by the river. He builds the Harpfe for his hay every summer, keeps his numbers in a little notebook and teaches his grandson Jakob to count the sacks. Until the village has a field he helps wherever there is work.

greet.de: Ah, du bist es. Grüß dich!
Servus! Heute mahle ich den Heiden.
greet.en: Hi! Today I'm grinding the buckwheat.
greet.it: Ciao! Oggi macino il grano saraceno.

greet.de: Da bist du! Ich habe die Säcke gezählt: zehn. Hilfst du mir?
greet.sl: Tu si! Preštel sem vreče: deset jih je. Mi pomagaš?
greet.en: There you are! I've counted the sacks: ten. Will you help me?
greet.it: Eccoti! Ho contato i sacchi: dieci. Mi aiuti?

greet.de: Schön, dass du da bist! Du gehörst schon zur Familie. Komm herein.
greet.sl: Lepo, da si tu! Zdaj si že del družine. Vstopi.
greet.en: Good to see you! You're family now. Come in.
greet.it: Che bello vederti! Ormai sei di famiglia. Entra, entra.

thanks.en: Thank you. A job well done.

thanks.de: Danke! Eins, zwei, drei Säcke: alles stimmt.
thanks.sl: Hvala! Ena, dve, tri vreče: vse je prav.
thanks.en: Thanks! One, two, three sacks: all correct.
thanks.it: Grazie! Uno, due, tre sacchi: tutto giusto.

thanks.sl: Hvala. S številkami ti gre dobro.
thanks.it: Grazie. Sei bravo con i numeri.

remember.de: Ich denke immer noch an {memory}. Immer.
Wenn ich die Säcke zähle, denke ich an {memory}.
remember.en: When I count the sacks, I think of {memory}.

idle.de: Das Heu ist trocken. Morgen kommt es auf die Harpfe.
idle.sl: Seno je suho. Jutri gre na kozolec.
idle.en: The hay is dry. Tomorrow it goes on the Harpfe.
idle.it: Il fieno è secco. Domani va sulla rastrelliera.

idle.de: Morgen regnet es. Ich spüre es in den Knien.
idle.sl: Jutri bo deževalo. Čutim v kolenih.
idle.en: It'll rain tomorrow. I can feel it in my knees.
idle.it: Domani piove. Lo sento nelle ginocchia.

idle.de: Hundert, zweihundert, dreihundert … So viele Körner!
idle.en: A hundred, two hundred, three hundred … So many grains!

cheer.de: Sehr gut! Du zählst besser als ich.
cheer.en: Very good! You count better than I do.

comfort.de: Macht nichts. Zählen wir noch einmal.
comfort.it: Non fa niente. Contiamo di nuovo.

listen.de: Hörst du die Mühle? Hör zu.
listen.en: Can you hear the mill? Listen.

bye.de: Pfiat di! Grüß mir den Jakob.
bye.sl: Pfiat di! Pozdravi mi Jakoba. (pfiat di: avstrijski pozdrav, adijo)
bye.en: Pfiat di! Say hello to Jakob for me. (pfiat di: Austrian for bye)
bye.it: Pfiat di! Salutami Jakob. (pfiat di: saluto austriaco, ciao)

liked.de: Oh! Woher weißt du das? Das mag ich am liebsten.
liked.sl: O! Kako si vedel? To imam najraje.
liked.en: Oh! How did you know? It's what I like best.
liked.it: Oh! Come lo sapevi? È la cosa che mi piace di più.

liked.de: Sehr gut! Genau das habe ich gebraucht.
liked.en: Very good! Exactly what I needed.
liked.it: Bravo! Proprio quello che mi serviva.

liked.de: Danke! Heute zähle ich nur schöne Sachen: eins!
liked.sl: Hvala! Danes štejem samo lepe stvari: ena!
liked.en: Thank you! Today I only count nice things: one!
liked.it: Grazie! Oggi conto solo le cose belle: una!

ordinary.de: Danke. Wir sind ja Nachbarn, nicht wahr?
ordinary.en: Thank you. We're neighbours, aren't we?

ordinary.de: Oh, danke. Das war nicht nötig.
ordinary.en: Oh, thank you. You didn't have to.

rare.de: Na so was! Das habe ich nicht erwartet. Vielen, vielen Dank!
rare.sl: No, kaj takega! Tega nisem pričakoval. Najlepša hvala!
rare.en: Well I never! I didn't expect that. Thank you so much!
rare.it: Questa poi! Non me l'aspettavo. Grazie mille!
